title: Controlled application to one agent
boundary: Off by default. Preparing and approving a binding does not wake an agent, start a model, authorize charges or send anything externally. Registry selection remains separate.
profile: Initial support: built-in Claude CLI, local environment, explicitly pinned company API-key version. Subscription, native, ACP, router, remote and configuration overlays are rejected, never silently converted.
scope: Only tasks created after approval, with no project, at their first fresh dispatch. Existing tasks, resumed sessions, retries, recovery and later wakes do not inherit this binding. The revision is appended literally; existing templates and instructions are not replaced. A later continuation may still retain the prompt already introduced in the session; rollback cannot erase that history.
visibility: Not private execution: prompt text may reach ordinary run logs, authorized tools, outputs, task comments and artifacts, and their authorized readers. Secret redaction does not keep prompt text private.
disabled: Application is disabled or has not been verified. No runtime binding can be approved here yet.
evidenceReady: An explicitly selected historical comparison is ready. Preparation revalidates its exact evidence and target.
evidenceNeeded: Compare historical tests above, then choose “Use for application review”. This does not prepare or approve anything automatically.
expiryBoundary: The deadline applies only to approving this proposal. A configured binding does not expire after 60 minutes; it remains until explicit rollback, with drift and permission checks at dispatch.
contextBoundary: Incomplete model context: this snapshot binds configuration and implementation, not complete model context. Private bare comparison is not proof of ordinary tool-enabled quality.
confirmOrdinaryVisibility: I accept the ordinary logs, tools, outputs, comments and artifact visibility described above.
confirmBareComparisonNotToolQuality: I understand that private bare comparison does not prove ordinary tool-enabled quality.
confirmNewTasksOnly: I confirm this one agent, the fixed revision and scope: new projectless tasks, first fresh dispatch only.
confirmNoAutomaticRun: I understand this configures a binding only; it does not start execution or authorize charges or external actions.
confirmRollback: Withdraw only this current binding for future eligible dispatches. Keep other agent configuration and secrets unchanged. This does not stop existing runs, release their leases, or undo past tool effects.
dispatchBoundary: Configured is not dispatched. A prepared receipt without a dispatch witness does not establish delivery of this literal to model stdin; ordinary metadata and logs may already contain the prompt. A dispatched receipt does not prove provider consumption. No receipt is not proof of no disclosure or execution.
inputUnconfirmed: Delivery to model stdin is unconfirmed
inputNotApplied: This literal was not delivered to model stdin
inputDispositionBoundary: A not-applied-before-input witness proves only that this literal was withheld from model stdin. Ordinary metadata or logs may already contain the prompt, and CLI-start effects may have occurred. Existing runs may continue; stopped status is unconfirmed. This does not stop runs or release their leases.
recover: Check the same request — read only
prepared: Proposal prepared, not configured. Inspect the current target, review the fixed digests and confirm all four boundaries before approving.
configured: A configuration receipt was recorded; it may be historical. No wake or execution was started by this action. Refresh to check the current binding and actual dispatch receipts.
rolledBack: Binding rolled back for future eligible dispatches. Other configuration and past effects are unchanged.
failed: Cannot verify this view. Private details were cleared. Check access and refresh; do not assume application succeeded.
storageFailed: Safe request metadata could not be stored or verified. Writes are blocked; do not clear storage to retry an uncertain action.
unknown: The write outcome is unknown. New requests are blocked. Query the same ID first; only an explicit, freshly confirmed retry may resend the identical request.
unresolved: No durable result is visible yet. This does not cancel a delayed write. Keep the request ID; query again or explicitly review and retry the exact request.
conflict: Target changed, evidence drifted, or execution is active. Nothing was overwritten. Stop active work separately if needed, then inspect current state and review a new proposal.
rejected: The server rejected this proposal or action. Check the supported profile, permissions and fixed evidence; nothing was silently converted.
noDispatches: No actual dispatch receipts are recorded for this application.
reviewRetry: Review the original proposal for an explicit retry
confirmRetry: I explicitly authorize resending this exact request ID and fixed payload, not creating a replacement. An existing success will only return its prior receipt.
retrySameRequest: Retry this exact request — never a new ID
abandonPrepareBoundary: Preparation never applies a binding or runs a model. This only removes local recovery metadata; a delayed server proposal may still be created and can appear in history. It does not cancel or approve that proposal. Never use this for uncertain approval or rollback.
abandonedPrepare: Local preparation recovery was abandoned. A server proposal may still exist, but no approval or execution was authorized.
notAppliedClosed: The server has proven this request was not applied and can no longer apply at its fixed generation or approval deadline. Local recovery is closed; inspect current state before making a new proposal.
credentialVersions: Pinned company credential IDs / versions (not secret values)
proposalVisibility: Preparing a proposal stores deployment metadata visible to this company’s authorized owners and administrators, including revision, dataset and test IDs and the cost cap. Private case text, results and prompt contents are not included in this metadata.
